location: SPEC.md > CAP-7 success; cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers (CAP-7) > Cross-engine lock
issue: The CAP-7 success criterion (both browser:<engine> phases start before either ends) is met even when the lock serializes everything. On bankwire, the universal smoke and 4 of the 5 specs have a BO goto, so they take the lock exclusive. The only FO-only spec, checkout-empty-banks, can overlap only with the other engine's copy of itself. The two browser phases therefore 'overlap' only as wall-clock spans, while the scenarios run almost fully serialized. Meanwhile every parallel boot adds snapshot-db plus lock-wait overhead.
implementation_impact: CAP-7 can pass its test and still make the bankwire release gate slower than sequential browsers (snapshot-db + lock-wait + extra worker processes). Nothing in the contract detects this, and the before/after timing report would show it only after the code is built.
suggestion: Change the CAP-7 success criterion to measure real concurrency, e.g. the summed scenario run time of both engines is greater than the version's wall-clock for browser driving, or lock-wait totals stay below a stated share of browser time. Also state the expected CAP-7 benefit on bankwire given its BO-heavy specs, or add a rule that falls back to sequential browsers when most scenarios are BO, to skip the snapshot-db cost.

location: SPEC.md > Success signal; cell-contract.md > Phase timings (CAP-6) last bullet; cell-contract.md > Aggregate
issue: The success signal takes the 'after' wall-clock of one fix-loop iteration from CAP-6 e2e_phase_durations. But the aggregate builds e2e_phase_durations only from the records it selected for the verdict: the newest gate-grade record, else the newest record. A warm fix-loop iteration is never gate-grade, so once any cold record exists for the cell, its timings never reach e2e_phase_durations. The 'before' side relies on progress-log START/END timestamps, but the progress log is truncated on every run (run-phases.md, cell-contract.md Phase timings). No step says when or how the baseline gets captured before the scripts change.
implementation_impact: The mandatory before/after report cannot be produced from the named sources. Implementers will either invent an ad-hoc extraction, or measure after the upgrade, when the 'before' scripts no longer exist.
suggestion: Name the source for warm-iteration timings (e.g. read phase_durations/boot_phases of the specific record from the cell history, not the aggregate). Add an explicit step: capture the 'before' numbers on bankwire with today's scripts before any script change lands, copying each progress log after each run. Define the measured unit for both sides (which layers count as part of a 'fix-loop iteration', image already pulled, same --jobs/slots, same host load).

location: cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers (CAP-7) > Parallel-only failures ('So no DB row, file, cache or opcode state written by the parallel pass can be confirmed as a failure')
issue: The rerun-seq reset deletes files that are absent from the snapshot, recopies modules/<mod>, and clears var/cache. It does not restore docroot files that existed at the snapshot and were modified by the parallel pass (e.g. .htaccess regenerated by a BO setting, theme or config files, overwritten images). The Warm container section admits this exact gap ('Files that existed at baseline and were modified are not restored'), but the CAP-7 text claims complete isolation. Also, rerun-seq does not re-run the module install. A failure that depends on install-time side effects that the parallel pass mutated is therefore not reset either.
implementation_impact: A finding produced by residue from the other engine's parallel pass can be 'confirmed' by rerun-seq and block the release gate. That breaks the identical-findings guarantee, and the live test will flake on modules whose BO scenarios rewrite existing files.
suggestion: Either state the same limitation as for the warm reset and weaken the CAP-7 'identical to sequential' claim, or extend the snapshot to record checksums (or mtime+size) of pre-existing docroot files and restore modified ones from a copy taken at snapshot time.

location: SPEC.md > CAP-7 success ('findings are identical to a sequential run'); cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers > Identical findings, Slots
issue: The reference 'sequential run' is undefined in a way that matters. In the --sequential-browsers fallback (and today's runner), the second engine runs on the DB that the first engine already mutated, with no reset between engines. In parallel mode, each failing engine is confirmed from a clean snapshot. bankwire relies on cross-engine state: checkout-with-bank's description says the second engine's add-bank POST fails duplicate validation and the checkout uses the first engine's bank row, and checkout-empty-banks assumes zero banks. So the outcome for engine 2 depends on the mode. Whether a version is admitted parallel or sequential depends on free slots, i.e. on host load.
implementation_impact: The same module and source can get different findings, and a different ready, depending on how many slots were free at admission. The identical-findings live test compares two modes with different state semantics, so it can fail or pass for reasons unrelated to the implementation.
suggestion: Define the sequential reference precisely (e.g. sequential mode also resets to the post-warmup-bo snapshot between engines), so both modes give each engine the same starting state. Apply that reset in the --sequential-browsers fallback too, and say so in cell-contract.md.

location: cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers > Parallel-only failures ('rerun failures the parallel pass did not report, are added to inconclusive'); cell-contract.md > Plan step 3 blocked-infra
issue: A failure that appears only in the sequential rerun is a conclusive, reproducible defect that the parallel pass hid (e.g. by FO-FO overlap or state from the other engine). The contract files it under `inconclusive`, so the cell becomes a pass with non-empty inconclusive (reason inconclusive-steps). Plan step 3 treats inconclusive-steps as an infra cause. Two such runs in one session give `blocked-infra`, which ends the E2E loop and reports a real module bug as an infrastructure problem.
implementation_impact: Real defects get mislabeled as infra and never enter findings. The operator is told to fix infrastructure, and the E2E loop stops without a loop-back to fix the bug.
suggestion: Give rerun-only failures their own channel (e.g. `sequential_only`) and a non-infra plan reason. Or treat a conclusive rerun failure as a blocking finding: it was produced sequentially from a clean snapshot, which is the confirmation standard the contract itself sets. Exclude that cause from blocked-infra.

location: cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers, second bullet (BO-login fallback '#2' pass); SPEC.md > Constraints ('Release-gate evidence comes only from cold boots') and Assumptions ('warm state can mask install-path bugs')
issue: When one engine's BO login fails in parallel mode, its result is discarded and replaced by a '#2' pass run after an in-place reset (reset-db/reset-files/reset-opcache, no reinstall). 'Only that pass counts, its findings need no sequential confirmation', and the record keeps boot: cold, so it is gate-grade. This is exactly the reset-container evidence that the constraints forbid for the gate (warm-like state, install not re-run). The record carries no marker that would let the plan or aggregate tell it apart.
implementation_impact: Release-gate evidence for a cell can come from a reset container rather than a cold boot, with no field that exposes this. That undermines the honesty law that the spec puts first.
suggestion: Mark such records (e.g. `boot: cold-reset` or a `reset_pass: true` field) and decide explicitly whether they are gate-grade. If not, have the plan schedule a cold single-browser run for that cell instead of accepting the #2 pass.

location: cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers > Cross-engine lock ('The wait has no timeout of its own'); references/headless.md (silence rule); run-phases.md (SLOW rule)
issue: lock-wait:<engine> has no deadline. If the holding engine hangs inside a scenario (crashed renderer, a Playwright driver hang, browser.close() blocking), the waiting engine waits forever and the version process never finishes. Both phases keep emitting ALIVE/SLOW heartbeats, so the headless '3 minutes without new line' stop rule never fires, and headless policy for SLOW is 'wait'. wait-slots for cells queued behind the run's own cells is also explicitly unlimited. Neither phase gets a SLOW threshold, so interactive runs will flag routine waits as 'suspected stall' after 180 s and offer to kill the job.
implementation_impact: A headless gate run can hang indefinitely. Interactive runs produce false stall alarms during normal tier-1 queueing and BO serialization, which pushes the operator toward stopping healthy jobs.
suggestion: Give lock-wait a bound derived from the holder's remaining scenario budget (or a per-worker overall deadline enforced by the version process, which kills the hung worker and records `crash`). Add per-phase SLOW thresholds (or exempt the phases) for wait-slots, lock-wait and rerun-seq in PROGRESS_SLOW_AFTER_PHASE, and update the stall guidance in run-phases.md and headless.md.

location: SPEC.md > Constraints (Headless) and tier-matrix.md > Rules ('stops at the first step that is not clean'); cell-contract.md > Configured cells / psm_e2e_canary
issue: The canary is fixed (newest version × chromium) and does not adapt to the host. If the canary cell cannot run for infra reasons (chromium binary missing, the 9.1 image absent while headless never pulls, a 9.1-only boot problem), tier 0 is never clean. Headless then returns at once and interactive ends in blocked-infra after two attempts. No other configured cell runs, even when its image and browser are available. Today the same run would still produce Firefox evidence and evidence for the other versions.
implementation_impact: Headless callers (psm-develop, psm-cross-version) get zero E2E evidence on any host where the canary cell has an infra problem, which is a regression in information compared to the current runner. Operators can only work around it by editing psm_e2e_canary by hand.
suggestion: Define a canary infra fallback: when the canary's newest record is inconclusive for an environment reason (browser-unavailable, missing image / errors before install), the plan picks the next configured cell as the acting canary for that session and reports it. Or at least state the regression and add the canary-unavailable case to the headless return contract.

location: cell-contract.md > Headless (return JSON gains versions, not_run_cells, e2e_tier_reached; early returns are status: complete); cell-contract.md > Docs to update at implementation
issue: The headless return contract changes meaning. A call now stops at the first unclean tier step and reports other versions as `not reached: stopped at <step>`. Each call mints a new session, so blocked-infra never fires across calls. The 'Docs to update' list covers only the cleanup-orphans part of references/headless.md (its Kembalian section is not listed). It names none of the four callers (psm-develop, psm-cross-version, psm-scaffold, psm-optimize), whose fix loops interpret the result.
implementation_impact: Callers keep reading the old per-version verdict semantics. A caller may treat `not reached` versions as failing (or passing), or loop forever re-calling psm-validate on a persistent infra cause, because every call starts a fresh session.
suggestion: Add references/headless.md 'Kembalian' (new fields, the not-reached meaning, the one-step-per-call behaviour) and each caller skill that consumes the verdict to the update list. State how a caller should react to `not reached` and repeated infra reasons across calls (e.g. pass the session token back in, or have the caller stop after N identical infra returns).

location: SPEC.md > CAP-1 intent; tier-matrix.md > Rules (Phase 1 loop ends only when V is clean); cell-contract.md > Plan > Phase 1, Phase 2 entry
issue: Phase 2 (tier 1, Layer 3, aggregate) starts only when every version is clean on Layers 1, 2 and 5 and tier 0 is gate or done. The only escape is 'E2E loop ended'. There is no defined exit for a blocking Layer 1/2/5 finding, or a canary E2E failure, that the operator cannot or will not fix in this session (false positive, accepted incompatibility, fixture problem). Today the operator can move on to Phase 2 and get an honest ready=false verdict with full evidence. Under this contract the interactive session never reaches the aggregate.
implementation_impact: Interactive sessions can deadlock in Phase 1 with no verdict file, no tier-1 evidence and no Layer 3 review. Implementers will add an undocumented operator bypass, which then has no defined effect on ready, the hosting loop or the session state.
suggestion: Define an explicit operator 'stop converging' action: it ends the loops, runs the Phase 2 steps that are still meaningful (Layer 3, merge-only, aggregate), records the stopped state the way 'E2E loop ended' does, and keeps ready=false. Also say whether tier 1 runs in that case.

issue: Histories are append-only and never compacted or rotated. Every plan call (several per fix-loop iteration) and every aggregate call parses every line of every configured cell's history, and each record carries findings, screenshots lists, boot_phases and keeper_boot. Over months of fix loops on one module, the files and the parse cost grow without bound. Nothing defines retention, or which records a compaction may safely drop given the 'newest gate-grade', 'recorded failure' and 'latest full-scenario record' rules.
implementation_impact: Plan latency and disk use grow over time. A later ad-hoc cleanup that drops old lines could silently change derivations: losing the failing record changes the focus cell, and losing the latest full record changes the failed set.
suggestion: Specify a compaction rule that keeps, per cell, the records every derivation can still select (newest record, newest gate-grade, newest cold full conclusive, newest conclusive, latest full-scenario, the last two records for blocked-infra) and drops the rest, run under the same LOCK_EX. Or set a retention bound and test that compaction does not change any plan output.

location: cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers > Cross-engine lock (FO-only scenarios shared) and Parallel-only failures (only engines with findings are rerun)
issue: Only engines that reported findings get rerun-seq. A scenario that passes in the parallel pass because the other engine's persistent writes changed its preconditions is never re-examined. The lock prevents overlap, not ordering-dependent state. On bankwire, whether engine B's checkout-empty-banks ('0 banks, early-return path') runs before or after engine A's checkout-with-bank adds a bank depends on scheduling. So the zero-bank path is exercised or skipped nondeterministically, and the record cannot show which happened.
implementation_impact: A cell's passing gate-grade evidence may not have covered the behavior its spec claims to cover, and the coverage differs from run to run. That is a false pass the honesty law is meant to exclude.
suggestion: Either reset to the post-warmup-bo snapshot per engine before each engine's first scenario that the other engine's BO writes could affect (simplest: run engines on separate DB copies, or separate shops/schemas), or document the limitation and require specs whose preconditions are global (e.g. 'no banks') to declare it, e.g. a spec field that forces sequential, reset-isolated execution.
